cards.b: May cause hypoadrenalism → cannot mount a response to surgical stress → an increased dose is usually needed (amount depends on the procedure). Signs of hypoadrenalism: hypotension/shock, hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia — look for them in any unwell steroid-dependent patient post-op; urgent steroids may be needed to avoid an Addisonian crisis

Withdrawal risks thromboembolic events, particularly MI. Do not withdraw before stent endothelialisation — takes up to 6 months. Weigh against surgical bleeding; if feasible, postpone surgery and withdraw only after consulting a cardiologist or vascular surgeon
Balance thromboembolic risk of stopping vs bleeding risk; NOACs need special peri-operative consideration; use of bridging anticoagulation
Depending on surgery and other VTE risk factors, it may be advisable to stop oestrogen-containing drugs 4–6 weeks beforehand — balanced against the risk of unwanted pregnancy
Serotonin syndrome with tramadol; ↑ bleeding with NSAIDs or warfarin
Narrow therapeutic index, renally excreted (accumulates in renal dysfunction), interacts with anaesthetic agents and muscle relaxants; arrhythmias, GI upset
Need not be stopped, but alert the anaesthetist (hypotension, arrhythmia)
Interact with opiates and vasopressors; ideally stop 2–3 weeks before surgery; in an emergency avoid opiates and pressor agents

delay elective non-cardiac surgery ~6 months (on DAPT) — matches the slide notes (endothelialisation takes up to 6 months); older keys: ~1 year and stop clopidogrel 5–7 days before. Never operate early or stop DAPT early for elective surgery
DDAVP (desmopressin) pre-op (uremic platelet dysfunction)
reschedule until euthyroid (risk of myxedema coma after surgery in hypothyroid patients)
agree with the surgeon who refused: uncontrolled diabetes = high risk (ASA 3); optimize first

it must be the patient's decision · all the information they "need to know" must be freely provided · the patient must be able to understand and apply the information · for consent to be valid it must be voluntary and informed, and the person consenting must have the capacity to make the decision.
